advisor/skills/advisor.note: adopt-skill — second-opinion consultation policy. Nothing in the corpus owns it and it cannot be housed without breaking one-home-per-rule: systematic-debugging escalates to the human partner and only after three failed fixes ('Three failures against one bug means the fixes shared an assumption that is wrong'); subagent-driven-development's Model Selection assigns a model per task, never consults one about a decision; requesting-code-review dispatches a reviewer for finished work, not a decision checkpoint. The transferable mechanism is the checkpoint set plus its budget: consult before a hard-to-reverse or wide-blast-radius decision (once you have a concrete plan, not before), when stuck or reaching for a workaround, and before declaring done; at most one follow-up per checkpoint, ~4 per task or the task should be split; the advisor is read-only and you stay accountable. Drop all Cursor machinery: `/advisor` commands, `.cursor/advisor/state.json`, stop hooks, and model slugs.

cli-for-agent/skills/cli-for-agents.note: adopt-skill — strongest find in the repo. Corpus coverage is zero (no skill mentions idempotency, --dry-run, exit codes, stdin, or help-text design; the only `--help` hits are an example finding inside a review prompt and a keyword note in writing-skills/references). No host exists: designing-component-systems owns component APIs, following-repo-ui-conventions owns repo UI, and neither reaches a command-line surface. Mechanism-dense and stack-agnostic: every input expressible as a flag with interactive as fallback rather than default; layered per-subcommand help so unused commands stay out of context; Examples with real invocations in every --help; fail fast on a missing flag with a correct example invocation instead of hanging; idempotency because agents retry; --dry-run for destructive actions with --yes to bypass confirmation while humans keep the safe default; consistent resource+verb structure; machine-useful success output (IDs, URLs, durations). Note the README's 'CLI and API surfaces owned by their publisher' row excludes documenting a vendor's CLI — not the craft of designing your own.

method: All 91 SKILL.md files enumerated from the tree at the pinned sha; every file carries exactly one disposition, asserted to sum to 91. 74 were assessed by three scout audits. The remaining 17 were initially dispositioned from descriptions alone, then read in full (plus 11 companion files), which overturned that verdict on 8 and produced 3 further adoptions. Two Benny rows outside those 17 were verified by targeted grep rather than a full read; their evidence fields say so.
caveat: Verdicts come from three scout audits of differing strictness. AuditPstackWorkflows applied a visibly laxer bar than AuditTeamKitThermos: it returned adopt-rule for workflow recipes with hardcoded model slugs (arena, architect, why, teach, figure-it-out) of the same class AuditTeamKitThermos rejected (review-and-ship, new-branch-and-pr). An independent oracle pass read 14 of the 19 unlanded adopt-rule rows and found roughly 20% survive as stated, 30-40% yield any edit at all, none yields a section. Treat adopt-* as a lead list, not a work queue.

statusMeaning.landed: Adopted into the corpus; landedIn names the destination.
statusMeaning.pending: adopt-* verdict from a scout audit, NOT yet assessed by the oracle pass or actioned. See `caveat` — roughly 20% survive scrutiny as stated. A lead, not a task.
statusMeaning.no-action: duplicate, reject, or product-specific. No corpus change warranted.
